title: Can you spot the net that can't fold?
desc:
Puzzle 1 of the Saturday puzzles: which of these nets won't fold into a cube? Pick A, B, C or D before the fold.

The answer is C. Four of its squares meet at one point, but every corner of a cube has only three faces, so when you fold it two faces crash into each other and one side is left open. In fact no cube net ever contains a 2×2 block of squares.

THE MATHS: there are 35 different shapes you can make from six squares joined edge to edge (hexominoes). Exactly 11 of them fold into a cube. We checked all 35 by computer, rolling a cube across each shape.

TRY IT: draw any of the 11 nets on squared paper, cut it out and fold it. Then try one with a 2×2 block and see where it jams.

Comment the letter you picked.
